title: Still singing “When the last ship sails!” on the daily tbh #broadway ...
transcript: If you don't have the context to understand this bizarre but delightful piece of news, let me explain. Because, like, what do you mean the failed Sting musical from 2014 is coming to the Metropolitan Opera for one week only starring sting himself and the reggae artist Shaggy? Going back to the beginning for a second, for those who don't remember, Sting had a flop Broadway musical in 2014 called The Last Ship, mostly based on his own story, and I was low key obsessed with it. I saw it twice, once before Sting joined the cast and once after. And I'll be the first to admit that the original book by John Logan and Brian Yorkey left a lot to be desired. Not least because the central plot point of the titular Last Ship is almost comically nonsensical if you think about it for more than five seconds. But I didn't care. I love this show anyway. I still found a lot of earnest emotional resonance in the story, and the score was really quite beautiful. It definitely deserved its Tony nomination, and it still holds up! The score was mostly original, by the way, but also included a handful of pre-existing songs in a pretty impressively seamless way. But despite its Broadway failures, Sting has been nothing if not persistent, (dare I say insistent) about keeping this passion project alive. The show has had a surprising number of major runs in the last 10 years or so. I believe this newest version is now the 3rd version of the book they've written, presented as kind of a mini international tour, I guess, with one of its [engagements] being New York City for nine performances only. And from what I can tell, this is being kind of hosted by the Met Opera, but not actually part of their season. Not totally out of left field when you consider there have been a few other international tours that utilized Lincoln Center venues when they came to New York, but I still think this is kind of a bizarre venue for this material. And then the announcement had the real double whammy sentence that the reggae artist Shaggy is playing the Ferryman, a role that did not exist in the Broadway production. I don't know if it was in the other version, but I like to imagine Shaggy was like, “hey buddy, can I come on tour with you?” and Sting was like, “I'm sure we can find something for you” And then, of course, Sting himself is returning to the supporting role of Jackie White, which he's played multiple times before, including as a replacement on Broadway. I have no idea if I'll actually think this is good, but as the #1 fan of the Broadway production and being very curious to see how it's evolved over the years, there's no way I'm missing this!
